title: Is working from home holding you back in your career?
description:
Working from home has plenty of benefits: no commute, greater flexibility and the chance to catch up on household chores during your break. But for young people starting out their careers, could this extra freedom actually have a negative impact on career progression?

Emer Moreau, a BBC Business Reporter, breaks it down. She explains how the pandemic led to a huge increase in at-home and remote working, and looks at how many people have now returned to in-person work.

She also discusses the impact working from home has on productivity, how it affects the social nature of working life, and the ways it can slow someone's effort to climb the career ladder. We also hear from young people about their experiences with remote working.

summaryZh: 節目討論疫情後在家工作（遠端/混合模式）帶來的利弊：好處包括免通勤與更大彈性，但對剛起步的年輕人或某些職務可能不利。記者 Eimear Moreau 提到疫情讓遠端工作成常態，現在仍有三億三千萬人 部分或完全遠端上班，且以科技、資訊、保險與金融業居多；年齡也是因子，十六至二十四歲族群 在家工作的比例較低。研究顯示遠端工作的生產力是混合結果：資淺、需高度協作的工作在家較容易降低產出，而從事較獨立研究或資深員工 在家時反而生產力提高。企業高層與部分 CEO 指出，缺乏辦公室能見度會妨礙升遷，Emma Greed 也指出女性因較少回辦公室而可能被落後。節目並訪問數位年輕人個案：軟體工程師 Vera 分享她從遠端起步，雖拿到提前升遷但必須花更多力氣記錄與展現成果；另有受訪者表示混合模式最理想，或雖喜歡在家工作但某些內容在辦公室較容易完成。報導建議年輕人主動提高能見度：每日主動聯繫、記錄工作成果、盡可能安排面對面或半面對面交流並多問問題，以縮短學習曲線與維持職涯動能。
summaryEn: The episode examines whether working from home can hinder career progression, especially for young or early-career workers. It notes the pandemic made remote work widespread and that about 330 million people still work remotely either part- or full-time, concentrated in tech, information, insurance and financial sectors; younger age groups are less likely to work remotely. Evidence on productivity is mixed: employers often worry remote staff are less productive, but research shows junior or highly collaborative roles tend to be less productive at home, while senior or more independent work can be more effective remotely. Leaders have warned that reduced visibility in the office can slow promotions—Emma Greed argued women who stayed away from offices have been disadvantaged. Personal accounts include a software engineer, Vera, who started remotely, won an out-of-cycle promotion but had to document and promote her work heavily; others prefer hybrid models for learning, confidence-building and collaboration. Practical tips given are to increase visibility (regular check-ins, documenting results), seek in-person contact where possible and ask more questions to accelerate learning and career growth.
